claims.statement: In January 1875 George Rooke of Newark, N.J., challenged Tom Allen to fight him for the championship of America for $2,500 a side.

claims.statement: Tom Allen authorized his friend Arthur Chambers to accept George Rooke's challenge.

thur Chambers, to aecept the challenge

claims.statement: Articles for the Allen-Rooke fight were drawn up and signed at Harry Hill's in New York on February 16, 1875.

claims.statement: The final deposit for the Allen-Rooke fight was made good at Harry Hill's on June 1, 1875, and John Chamberlin was chosen final stakeholder.

claims.statement: One of Rooke's backers sued Harry Hill for Rooke's share of the stakes, and Chamberlin declined to have anything to do with the affair.

claims.statement: Harry Hill telegraphed Arthur Chambers on May 16, 1875 that a formal demand had been made for Rooke's $1,500 share and that Rooke's backer threatened to sue Hill.

claims.statement: Tom Allen entered the ring at Smith's Landing at 10 a.m. on Thursday, June 17, 1875, before about 500 spectators, and remained until 1 o'clock.

claims.statement: A reply to Allen's telegram, apparently from Harry Hill, said the stakeholder would not pay Rooke's share to his backers unless compelled by law.

claims.statement: Tom Allen left Pittsburg on Friday, June 18, 1875, and arrived back in St. Louis the next morning.

claims.statement: Tom Allen announced his final withdrawal from the ring, saying he would make no more matches.
